_doc: The town's script (townsfolk step 8, #1144; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5 'What they say'). The same shape as no_law.json (docs/scripts/README.md): `cast` the pools (townsfolk share pools by type, DESIGN §9; cast ids shared with no_law.json keep one voice), `scenes` with `lines` (id, speaker, trigger, when, condition, delivery, words, takes). Lines may hold slots in braces ({who}, {whom}, {where}, {shots}, {teller}); a scene's `reads` says which code reads it. The `runner` and `news` scenes are read by the game now (TownScript, src/people/town_script.gd; a wording `built` is what the game said before this file, kept); the rest wait for step 9's line picker. Every wording is PROPOSED and nothing is voiced until Sean taps Script OK. No line here says Harlan's name. No Law's town, morning and funeral lines stay in no_law.json and aren't repeated.

cast.name: A townsman
cast.bible: P·bible (No Law's Beat 1, the town without a sheriff)
cast.brief: Forties, a storekeeper type; worried, talks low, glances over his shoulder.

cast.name: A townswoman
cast.brief: Thirties to forties, plain-spoken, good grammar; brisk, says what she thinks.

cast.name: A bold man in the street
cast.bible: No Law's Beat 1: 'others behave more boldly'
cast.brief: Thirties, a teamster or a hand in town; too loud, a little drunk, enjoying the sheriff's absence.

cast.name: The barkeep
cast.brief: Forties, aggrieved and quick, always counting what a thing costs him; a nasal Midwestern voice that rises when he's upset.

cast.name: The undertaker
cast.brief: Sixties, unhurried, precise, a dry gallows humour he doesn't know he has.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

cast.name: The storekeeper
cast.brief: Fifties, a Missouri man, careful with money and with words; polite to the penny. Says less when he's frightened, not more.

cast.name: The hotel's landlady
cast.brief: Forties, a widow who runs the hotel; brisk, plain, has fed worse men than these. Never raises her voice.

cast.name: The liveryman
cast.brief: Fifties, horse-sense and no patience; counts feed in nickels (#1184).

cast.name: The smith
cast.brief: Forties, big and slow-spoken; proud of his iron, shy of his letters (#1184).

cast.name: The drifter
cast.brief: Twenties, out of work and easy about it; rode in from nowhere much (#1184).

cast.name: The saloon girl
cast.brief: Twenties, quick and tired; teases, sizes a man up by his purse (#1184).

cast.name: The town drunk (Sarge)
cast.brief: Late fifties, a broken Union first sergeant from central Illinois; hoarse and carrying, fast and loud drunk, short and exact sober; crude about the body, never about a woman, and every joke has him getting the worst of it too.

scenes.title: The runner
scenes.when: Any day, a man down in town
scenes.reads: FetchHelp (src/people/fetch_help.gd): the most specific id that has words first (runner.shot, then runner); a wording by the runner's own seed. {where} is FetchHelp.place_name: 'the store', 'the saloon', 'Doc's'.
scenes.setting: A townsman who saw a man go down runs for the doctor (or, once there's a deputy, for Harlan), tells him on arrival, and hands over his version of the news.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He starts for the doctor's (Reaction's runner)
lines.delivery: Called back over his shoulder as he goes. The first words are to the others.

words.text: I'll get Doc! Don't move him.
I'll go. Don't move him.
Somebody fetch Doc... I'll go!
Leave him lay. I'm going for Doc.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He starts for Harlan (the badge given, Harlan seen in town)
lines.delivery: Over his shoulder, already going.

words.text: I'll get the deputy!
Somebody get the law... I'll go!
Where's the deputy? I'll find him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man was shot and is breathing
lines.delivery: Blown from the run; the place first, then that he's alive.

Doc, come quick! Man shot by {where}. He's breathing.

lines.delivery: As above.

lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man was shot and isn't breathing
lines.delivery: He knows the run was for nothing and comes anyway.

lines.delivery: As above.

words.text: Doc! There's a man dead by {where}.
Doc, there's a man lying dead at {where}. I don't know what done it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches Harlan (day 2 on): a man shot
lines.delivery: Says 'Deputy' like a man still getting used to it.

words.text: Deputy! Down at {where}, quick! A man's shot.

Deputy! There's a man shot at {where}.

lines.trigger: He reaches Harlan: a man down, not shot
lines.delivery: As above.

words.text: Deputy! You'd best come. There's trouble at {where}.

scenes.title: The news, as a man has it
scenes.when: Any day, the hours and the morning after a shooting
scenes.reads: TownNews.line_of (src/people/town_news.gd) builds a man's line from his own version: one head line by what he holds (a killing, a shooting, a man down, shots), then at most one of 'who drew first' or 'how many shots', then who told him. The most specific id with words first (news.killing.you, then news.killing); a wording by his seed, so three men who counted three shots say it three ways. Slots: {who} who fired (by TownNews.name_of: Earl, Cody, Doc, 'the new man' or 'the deputy', else 'the storekeeper'), {whom} who was hit ('a man' if he doesn't know), {where}, {shots} ('three shots'), {teller}. A sentence that starts with a slot gets its capital.
scenes.setting: A calm townsman near Harlan says his own news once, before his ordinary line; two townsmen telling each other say the same lines to each other. A version is only what that man sensed: a slot he didn't fill isn't spoken.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan killed a man; said to Harlan's face
lines.delivery: Not an accusation. He's telling the man what the town has, to see what the man does with it.

words.text: You shot {whom} dead, by {where}.

You shot {whom} dead at {where}. I was there.

{whom}'s dead. {who} shot him, by {where}.

lines.delivery: He doesn't know, and minds not knowing.

words.text: Somebody's killed {whom}, by {where}.
{whom}'s been shot dead at {where}. Nobody's saying who.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan shot a man who lived; to his face
lines.delivery: As news.killing.you.

words.text: You shot {whom} by {where}.
You put a ball in {whom}, by {where}.

lines.trigger: His version: a man shot, who did it

A man went down by {where}. I never saw what took him.

words.text: Shooting, down by {where}. {shots}.

Somebody was shooting, out by {where}. {shots}, near as I could tell.

You. Shooting {at}, like a damn fool. {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: shots, nobody hit, and he saw who fired (#1213: witnesses said 'whoever it was')

words.text: {who} let off his iron {at}. {shots}.
It was {who}, shooting {at}. {shots}. I saw him.
{who} fired, {at}. {shots}, and nobody hurt, thank God.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version, told where it happened: shots, nobody seen hit, the shooter unseen (#1213: 'down by the saloon' from inside it)
lines.when: shots only; who empty; at the place

words.text: Shooting, right here. {shots}.
Somebody fired, right here. {shots}.
There was shooting right here. {shots}. Never saw who.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, and he saw it
lines.delivery: He'll say it to anyone. He'd say it to a judge.

words.text: {whom} drew first. I saw it.
{whom} drew first. I'll swear to that.
It was {whom} drew first. I seen him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, by what he heard

words.text: {whom} drew first, I heard.
{whom} drew first, the way I heard it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, by what he was told

words.text: {whom} drew first, is what I'm told.
They say {whom} drew first.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: more than one shot, and he heard them
lines.delivery: The number is his: he counted.

words.text: {shots}, I counted.
{shots}. I counted them.
I made it {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: more than one shot, by what he was told

words.text: {shots}, they say.
{shots}, I'm told.
They say {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: who told him
lines.delivery: Last, a little offhand.

words.text: {teller} told me.
I had it from {teller}.
That's what {teller} says, anyhow.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Opening a telling to another townsman (mostly walla under it)
lines.delivery: One clear opener; the rest is murmur.

words.text: You heard what happened?
You hear? Last night.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Asked (a look held at him), his version's slots empty

words.text: I only heard it. I never saw a thing.
Don't ask me. I was indoors with the shutters to.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan shoved a man (#1272); {whom} is 'me' from the man shoved
lines.when: rough; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Not a challenge. He wants you to know it was seen.

words.text: You put hands on {whom}, {at}. I don't forget a thing like that.
That was you, shoving {whom} about, {at}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan shoved a man (#1272)

words.text: {who} shoved {whom} about, {at}.
{who} put hands on {whom}, {at}. No call for it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a man shoved, who did it dropped in the telling (#1272)

words.text: Somebody shoved {whom} about, {at}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan took a pot at the card table (#1279)
lines.when: cards won_pot; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Half sore, half admiring.

words.text: You took that pot off us, {at}. Don't make a habit of it.
Saw you clean up at cards, {at}. Lucky hand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan took a pot at the card table (#1279)

words.text: {who} took a pot at cards, {at}. Cleaned the table out.
{who} won a pot off Earl, {at}. Earl didn't care for it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan raised on nothing and was shown up (#1279)
lines.when: cards bluff_called; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Grinning at you.

words.text: Raised on nothing at cards, {at}. We all saw your hand, mister.
That bluff of yours, {at}. Nothing but nerve.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan's bluff at cards was shown up (#1279)
lines.delivery: Telling it as a joke.

words.text: {who} tried a bluff at cards, {at}. Caught with nothing in his hand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan caught {whom} dealing from the bottom (#1279); {whom} is 'me' from the cheat
lines.when: cards cheat_true; who Harlan; told to him

words.text: You caught {whom} dealing off the bottom, {at}. Somebody had to.
That was you called the cheat on {whom}, {at}. Good eyes.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan caught {whom} cheating at cards (#1279)

words.text: {who} caught {whom} dealing off the bottom, {at}.
{who} called {whom} a cheat at cards, {at}, and he was one.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan called {whom} a cheat and he wasn't (#1279); {whom} is 'me' from the man called
lines.when: cards cheat_false; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Cold.

words.text: You called {whom} a cheat, {at}. Never proved a thing.
Calling {whom} a cheat, {at}. Them's hard words, mister.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan called {whom} a cheat and it wasn't so (#1279)

words.text: {who} called {whom} a cheat at cards, {at}. Never proved a thing.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan stood the house a round (#1292)
lines.when: bar round; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Warm.

words.text: You stood us all a drink, {at}. Decent of you.
You bought for the house, {at}. I ain't forgot.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan stood the house a round (#1292)

words.text: {who} stood the house a round, {at}.
{who} bought for the whole bar, {at}. Free with his money.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Harlan was drunk (#1292)
lines.when: bar drunk; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Not unkind.

words.text: You were drunk as a lord, {at}.
You could hardly stand, {at}. I saw it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan was drunk (#1292)
lines.delivery: Telling it as a joke.

words.text: {who} got good and drunk, {at}.
{who} was falling about drunk, {at}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: the deputy drinking on duty (#1292)
lines.when: bar deputy; who Harlan; told to him
lines.delivery: Disapproving.

words.text: You were drinking on duty, {at}. With that badge on.
Badge on and a glass in your hand, {at}. I saw.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: the deputy drinking on duty (#1292)

words.text: {who} was drinking on duty, {at}, badge and all.
{who} wears the badge and drinks on duty, {at}.

scenes.title: The morning after, about Harlan
scenes.when: The day after Harlan shot a man in town
scenes.reads: Step 9 (regard and the barks) picks these by StoryState news.harlan, set overnight by TownNews: stopped_a_killer (the man he shot fired first, or had shot someone), shot_a_man, split (near even). Said as Harlan passes, or to him; only by a man whose own version has Harlan in it.
scenes.setting: Main Street, the morning after. No line names him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; his view stopped_a_killer
lines.delivery: A touch of the hat; he isn't used to praising anybody.

words.text: Heard he pulled on you first. Nobody's grieving him.
Morning. That was a bad one you put down.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; stopped_a_killer
lines.delivery: Half to him, half to the woman beside her.

words.text: He'd shot one already, they say. Before you stopped him.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: Harlan at the bar; stopped_a_killer
lines.delivery: Sets a glass down, and keeps his hand on the bottle.

words.text: This one's mine to stand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; his view shot_a_man (not to his face)
lines.delivery: Said once Harlan is past, loud enough.

words.text: That's him. Shot a man in the street.
Shot him before he'd cleared leather, I heard.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: Harlan near; shot_a_man
lines.delivery: To a boy at the window, not to Harlan.

words.text: Come away from there. Come inside.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.trigger: Harlan at his counter; shot_a_man
lines.delivery: Doesn't look up from the ledger.

words.text: I'll have the money first, if it's the same to you.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; the town split

words.text: Depends who you ask. Some say the other fellow pulled first.
I heard it both ways. I don't know as I believe either.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; split; the loudmouth on the walk
lines.delivery: To the whole walk.

words.text: I was told the fellow drew. Then I was told he never. Ask the deputy, he was stood right there, and I'd ask him myself only I'm busy.

scenes.title: The uneasy day
scenes.when: The day after a killing or a shooting the town holds (the calendar's `uneasy`)
scenes.reads: Step 9: barks by the day kind `uneasy` (valley_folk.json's kinds; StoryState news.yesterday = killing / shooting). Not after a story act's killing (No Law's morning is its own script).
scenes.setting: The storekeeper keeps in, the loudmouth's out on the walk telling it, the street's thinner.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.trigger: Shutting at 17:00
lines.delivery: Turning the sign, the bar in his other hand.

words.text: I'm barring the door tonight. You'd do the same.
Shutting early. It's nothing against you.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Wearing a pistol, at a lean spot
lines.delivery: Keeps touching it.

words.text: Never had cause to wear one in town before.
The wife made me put it on.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: On the walk, anyone within 4 m

words.text: Somebody ought to do something about it, and I said so, I said it to the storekeeper this morning.
I'd have stopped it, if I'd been there. I was at my supper.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: Calling children in, before noon

words.text: You stay in the yard today, you hear me?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: At the store's bench

words.text: Nobody's out. Even the dogs are under the porch.

scenes.title: The undertaker comes for a man
scenes.when: Any day, a man dead in town (ValleyFolk takes him to the undertaker's)
scenes.reads: When the undertaker's walk to a body is built (today the dead go once unseen, step 7's open), these are his: {whom} from his own version. No Law's Earl has his own lines (no_law.json morning.undertaker).
scenes.setting: The undertaker is exact; to him a dead man is a box, a name for the book and somebody to send the bill to.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: Arriving at the body
lines.delivery: Already measuring him with his eye.

words.text: Stand away, please. Somebody take his feet.
I'll have him now. Mind his head on the step.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; his version has whom
lines.delivery: Writing it down.

words.text: {whom}. Shot. I'll want his other name for the book, if anybody has it.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; nobody knows him
lines.delivery: Looks round the ring of faces; nobody.

words.text: Anybody know him? No. Then he goes in the book as a stranger, and the county pays.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; Harlan near and the undertaker's version has Harlan firing
lines.delivery: Not unkind. He only wants it right for the book.

words.text: Yours, Deputy? I'll put it down that way.

scenes.title: An ordinary day

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: You pass, before 10

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: At a lean spot, noon

lines.speaker: storekeeper

scenes.title: Trouble in the street
scenes.when: Any day, shots or a fight

lines.speaker: townsman

scenes.title: The town drunk has a go at the deputy
scenes.when: Any day once Harlan wears the badge
scenes.reads: TownDrunk (#1312): `jibe.first` once for good, then `jibe` once a meeting, the most specific that fits (what he sees on Harlan and the town knows of his day: `you`; the story's facts; the hour; his band; `sober`), each once a game day; Harlan's answers `jibe.nod`, `jibe.shake`, `jibe.shove`, `jibe.drink` (the sober lines, once each for good) then `jibe.drink.again`, `jibe.lead`, `jibe.let_go`, `jibe.jail`; the man by who hears it `jibe.heard` by his band. `gag` marks the running jokes Sean asked for (britches, pecker, bachelor).
scenes.setting: The saloon's walk, the store's bench, the jail's walk; the bar's door end at night. He never says the deputy's name (Brevet, farmer); nothing about Joe; no slurs; Rourke and the place in Tennessee not before Payday Night.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: The first time he sees the badge on you: always his first

words.text: Well, look at this. A brevet! That's Army, farmer: all of the rank and none of the pay, and nobody bound to mind you. Salute me, Brevet, I outrank you sober.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: You walk like a man with the quickstep and no sink dug. Ease off, Brevet, nobody's shooting yet.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Took a ball in the seat at Shiloh. Going forward! I'd bent for my cap. Surgeon said it was the one part of me he could find to hit.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Dress your line, Brevet! You're a line of one and you're still crooked.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: You got the look of a man fixing to load his breeches. I'd know. I've loaded mine in four states and a territory.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Find the necessary before you find the trouble, Brevet. I say it as a man downwind.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Look at him stand there, all neck and legs, like a shitepoke. You know why they call it that? Flush one and see. Flush you and we'd all see.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Hundred men jumped when I spoke, Brevet. Course, I spoke mostly when the shells come over.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Big star, big pistol, big hat. I'm adding it up, Brevet, and somewheres you come out short.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Holster hangs low on you, Brevet. Lower than anything else on you hangs, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: In the Army we had a word for a man with a big sword and a little pecker. Colonel.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Never seen you with a woman, Brevet. Confirmed bachelor, are you? I was one four years, in the Army. You get used to a man snoring in your ear. Then you get to missing it.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Pretty fellow like you wearing the star. I was pretty once, Brevet. A corporal proposed. I said I'd think on it, and I'm thinking still.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: No wife, no sweetheart, never once up the saloon's stairs. The whole street's wondered, Brevet. The girls upstairs have quit wondering.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Any meeting once you wear the badge

words.text: Boots blacked and hair combed, and not a woman in town to see it. Who's it for, Brevet? Don't tell me. I'll guess, and it'll be worse.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: His own band of you: wary

words.text: Here's the Brevet. Mind the step, it's higher than a furrow.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: His own band of you: cold

words.text: Don't stand there. You're keeping the sun off a veteran.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: His own band of you: afraid

words.text: Go on, then. I been hit by provosts. You'll do it softer.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: His own band of you: warm

words.text: Brevet! I'll say this for you. No, I won't, the street's listening. Go on with you.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Warm, and sober

words.text: Brevet. I'd salute, only I'm sober and it wouldn't be respectful.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Morning, sober
lines.delivery: Short, low; no salute.

words.text: Morning. I ain't drunk yet, so this don't count. Come back after ten and I'll tell you what I think of you.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Morning, sober

words.text: Too early, Brevet. I can't be funny about you on an empty stomach. On a full one neither, but I can try.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Noon

words.text: Noon, Brevet! I been drunk two hours and you ain't done a thing yet. One of us is working.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: The afternoon

words.text: Sweating under that star, Brevet? You sweat like a recruit at his first inspection. He'd at least washed.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Evening

words.text: Evening, Brevet. I been lit since noon, and you're only now lighting the lamps.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Night

words.text: Out on your rounds this hour? I'll come along. I know every place in town a man can fall down in the dark.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A shot came near you today

words.text: Heard the shooting, Brevet. Heard you too. Fresh pair of inexpressibles, is it? Go on, I won't tell nobody. I'll shout it.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You ran from a shot today

words.text: I seen you skedaddle, Brevet! Lord, you can run. Like a man that's left something behind him, and he has.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You ran from a shot today

words.text: Two kinds of soldier when the balls fly. Them as stands, and them as shit their britches and run. I was the third kind. Done both.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're running

words.text: Where's the fire, Brevet? Or is it the backhouse? Run, man! You'll never make it. I never did.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Your gun's out

words.text: Put that up before you hurt yourself. Last man I saw wave one like that shot his own foot and shat his britches, in that order. Or t'other.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Your gun's out

words.text: Whoa! Put it away, Brevet, there's ladies on the street. ... Oh, the pistol. Well, put that away too.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Blood on you, not yours

words.text: Somebody else's blood on you, Brevet. Good. Last time I come home bloody it was mine, and Doc wanted paying.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You were down on the ground today

words.text: Dirt all down your back, Brevet. Back of the britches too. I won't ask which end hit first.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You were down on the ground today

words.text: Seen you go down in the street. You went down like I go down, only I meant it.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're drunk

words.text: Drunk on duty! I'd have you in the guardhouse, Brevet, only I'm in it Thursdays myself.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're drunk

words.text: Look at him weave! That's my walk, Brevet. Took me twenty years to get it. Get your own.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're drunk

words.text: Drunk! Now you're a soldier, Brevet. Took me two years to get that look. You done it in an afternoon.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A glass in your hand

words.text: That glass don't suit you, Brevet. Hand it here. Some men's built for whiskey, and I'm built round it.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You lost at cards today

words.text: Lost at cards! I'd have lent you my luck, Brevet, only I lost that at cards too.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You lost at cards today

words.text: They cleaned you out at the table. Should have asked me. I can read your face from across the street, and I can't read.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You won a pot today

words.text: Won a pot, did you? Stand a veteran a drink out of it and I'll swear you never dealt off the bottom.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You won a pot today

words.text: Won a pot! First thing you've took off a man since you come here, Brevet. Excepting the sheriff's star.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Your bluff was called today

words.text: Tried a bluff at cards and got caught. You couldn't bluff a dog off a porch, Brevet. Nor can I. That's why I drink.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You shoved a man today

words.text: Seen you shove a man about. Good for you, Brevet. Pick one your own size. I'm free Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You shoved a man today

words.text: There's the bully of the street! I been shoved about by better. I been shoved by a brigadier, and he was drunker than me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You shot a man today

words.text: Shot a man today. Took you long enough. Army give me forty rounds at Shiloh and I come home with thirty-nine and a dent in my canteen.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You fired today and hit nobody

words.text: Heard you let off a round. Hit anything? Course not. You was aiming.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A blast near you today

words.text: Something blowed up. Was that you, Brevet? Or did you eat at the hotel?

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You arrested a man today

words.text: Took a man in alive! I'd have give odds on him taking you. I did give odds. I'm out a dime.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You stood the house a round today

words.text: Stood the house a round, and me out on the walk! I'll drink what they left in the glasses come morning. Your health, Brevet, a day late.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're carrying a man

words.text: Carry him gentle, Brevet. I carried men two years. Dropped one in a creek once and he thanked me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You read one of his notes today

words.text: Been reading the walls, Brevet? Educational, ain't they. Somebody in this town can spell 'pecker'. Weren't me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You read one of his notes today

words.text: Somebody's been writing things about you on the jail. I'd rub 'em out for you, only they're true and I'm short of chalk.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You walked him to the jail last night or today

words.text: Slept in your jail, Brevet. Cot's softer than you'd think. Softer than you, which I did think.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Sober, the morning after you walked him to the jail, the sheriff buried (his card's)
lines.delivery: Low and short. No joke in it.

words.text: He left that door unlocked six winters. Never said a word about it. I don't know what you mean to do.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: The sheriff dead

words.text: Sheriff's buried and you're wearing his tin. I wore a dead man's boots once. They pinched too, and I kept 'em.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: The sheriff dead

words.text: Sheriff stood up to that bunch with a ball in his belly. You'd want a bucket and a clean pair, Brevet.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: The sheriff dead

words.text: Doc says the sheriff picked you himself. Man was dying, Brevet. Dying men pick queer. I seen one ask for his mother and a peach.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You missed the sheriff's funeral

words.text: Didn't see you up the hill at the burying. Busy? I was busy too. Crying in a bottle. But I went, and I took the bottle.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You watched the funeral from off

words.text: Watched the burying from the lane, I hear. Like a picket. Afraid he'd sit up and ask for his star back?

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You sat at the table through Earl's murder (his card's knows)

words.text: Man shot dead across the table and you sat there like a recruit at church. I was by the door. I never moved neither, but I'm drunk.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You carried Earl to the doctor's

words.text: Carried Earl clear up the street, they say. I'd have helped, only I was holding the door. From the inside.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: No Justice ended in an arrest

words.text: Brought the one from the hills in alive! I never brought a man in alive in four years. Mostly they brought me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: No Justice ended without an arrest

words.text: Rode out after a man and come home without him. Lost him? I lost a whole company once. Still turning up, some of 'em.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan answers a jibe with a nod

words.text: He agrees! The Brevet agrees with me! Somebody chalk it up.
There, he nods. Even the Brevet's heard about the Brevet.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan answers a jibe with a nod

words.text: Nodding at me like a mule at a gate. I like a mule.
He takes it! Like the beans at Corinth, and it'll come out the same way.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan answers a jibe with a nod

words.text: Own it, Brevet. I owned mine. Mine's in a ditch outside Corinth.
Good man. I'll be kinder tomorrow. I won't, but it's a nice thing to hear.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan answers a jibe with a shake

words.text: Shaking your head? Careful, Brevet, it's the only one you got and it's half empty.
No, he says! Half the street heard it, Brevet, and the other half's coming.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan answers a jibe with a shake

words.text: Don't shake it so hard, it'll come off. Then where'd you hang your hat?
You say no. Your britches say otherwise.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan shoves or kicks him

words.text: Ha! Struck a veteran! Go on, there's room on the other side.
That's it, shove the old soldier. I been shoved by Johnny Reb, I can stand a farmer.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan shoves or kicks him; cold

words.text: Do that again and I'll tell the whole street you done it. I'll tell it better than it was.
Had a provost shove me once, Brevet. He's dead now. Not me that done it. Fevers.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan shoves or kicks him

words.text: Knocked me flat and never spilt a drop. That's training, Brevet. That's twenty years.
Easy! I'm the only man in town says it to your face. You'd miss me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan stands him a drink (the glass given him, or a round with him in the room): the first few times, a sober line, once each for good
lines.delivery: Sober inside the sentence. No salute.

words.text: Obliged. The night they shot Earl I was at the door end. I seen the stranger hold a man in his chair with a word. Nobody's asked me. You could, before ten.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan stands him a drink (the glass given him, or a round with him in the room): the first few times, a sober line, once each for good
lines.delivery: Sober for as long as it takes to say it.

words.text: Thank you. I mean it, and I'll deny it. Don't let 'em move you off the walk, Brevet. They moved me.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan stands him a drink (the glass given him, or a round with him in the room): the first few times, a sober line, once each for good
lines.delivery: Quiet; then louder, to cover it.

words.text: You never preached at me when you done that. Sheriff never did neither. ... There. That's all you get.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan stands him a drink (the glass given him, or a round with him in the room): the first few times, a sober line, once each for good
lines.delivery: Looking at the glass, not at you.

words.text: A man stood me a drink the night before Corinth and I never saw him after. Drink yours slow, Brevet.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A drink stood him, after the sober lines

words.text: Your health, Brevet! And mine, which is worse.
God bless the Union, the Republic, and the fool that pays.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A drink stood him, after the sober lines

words.text: Now that's a deputy. I take back near half of it.
Down the hatch. I'll think of something worse about you directly.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: A drink stood him, after the sober lines

words.text: Obliged, Brevet. I'll go easy on you till sundown.
Pour a veteran a drink and he's yours for an hour. Two, if it's the good.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: G at him: Harlan walks him to the jail

words.text: Arresting a veteran! On what charge? Drunk? Guilty. Lead on, Brevet.
Where we going? The jail? I know the way. I been carried it.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: G at him: Harlan walks him to the jail

words.text: I'll come quiet. Quieter than you'd go.
March me, then. Left! Left! ... You ain't got a left, Brevet. You got two rights and a stagger.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: Harlan lets him go on the way (G again, or walks off)

words.text: Lost your prisoner, Brevet. Happens to the best. Never happened to me, mind. I was always the prisoner.
Done with me? I'll be on the walk. I'm always on the walk.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: At the jail's door: in he goes to sleep it off

words.text: Leave the door off the latch. He always did.
Cot's still warm from the last fool. That was me, too.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: At the jail's door: in he goes to sleep it off

words.text: Don't lock it, Brevet. I'd only holler, and I got the voice for it.
Night, Brevet. Don't let the graybacks bite.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; cold: he laughs
lines.delivery: A laugh first.

words.text: Ha! He's got your number, Deputy.
Give it him, Sarge!

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; cold: she laughs
lines.delivery: Behind her hand.

words.text: Oh! I shouldn't laugh.
Well. Somebody had to say it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; wary: he winces

words.text: Lord, Sarge.
That's enough now, Sarge.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; wary: she winces

words.text: Must he?
That man. Every morning of the week.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; warm: he tells him to hush

words.text: Hush, Sarge. He's doing what he can.
Leave him be, Sarge. Go sleep it off.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe; warm: she tells him to hush

words.text: Ephraim Tolliver, you hush.
Pay him no mind, Deputy. Nobody does.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe: the barkeep

words.text: That'll do, Sarge.
Sarge. Inside, or quiet.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: A man by hears Sarge's jibe: Rufe, who's the less funny and knows it

words.text: That ain't even funny, Sarge.
I'd have said it louder.

lines.speaker: town_drunk
lines.trigger: You're hurt

words.text: Hit, are you? Show me. ... Lord, that's nothing. I been kicked worse by a mule, and the mule said sorry.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: Sarge had a go at him (#1312)

words.text: Sarge had a go at you again, {at}. Pays to let it go by.
Heard Sarge on at you {at}. He's like that with everybody. More with you.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Sarge had a go at the deputy (#1312)

words.text: Sarge had a go at {who} again, {at}.
The old soldier was on at {who} again, {at}. The whole walk heard it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Told to Harlan's face: Harlan stood Sarge a drink (#1312)

words.text: You stood Sarge a drink, {at}. He won't say thank you. He means it.
Bought Sarge one, {at}. He'll be easier on you. For a day.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan stood Sarge a drink (#1312)

words.text: {who} stood Sarge a drink, {at}.
{who} bought the old soldier a whiskey, {at}. Never preached at him, neither.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Told to Harlan's face: Harlan walked Sarge to the jail (#1312)

words.text: You walked Sarge to the jail, {at}. Sheriff used to do that, cold nights.
Put Sarge in the jail to sleep it off, did you? {at}, I heard.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan walked Sarge to the jail (#1312)

words.text: {who} walked Sarge off to the jail, {at}, to sleep it off.
{who} took Sarge to the jail {at}. Sheriff did that, winters.
